# Capped signed exponentials: at most one fractional positive coefficient

Let E_0,...,E_d be independent standard exponential variables. On the compact set

    A_d={a in[-1,1]^(d+1): a_0=-1, sum_i a_i=0},

put P(a)=Pr(sum_i a_i E_i>=0). This note proves a positive-side reduction for minimizing P. It is not a proof of the mixed-integer conjecture.

## The free-sign stratum theorem

At a local minimum of P on A_d, if at least one coefficient lies in (-1,0), then at most one coefficient lies in (0,1).

The fixed coordinate a_0 is not counted as free. Any other saturated negative coefficients, saturated positive coefficients, and zero coefficients may occur.

### Existence and regularity

P is continuous on A_d. Indeed, coefficients converging to a give almost-sure convergence of their signed sums when coupled with the same exponentials. The limiting sum has no atom at zero: the fixed term -E_0 is independent of the remaining terms and has a continuous law. Bounded convergence then gives continuity of the probabilities. Hence a global minimum exists.

For the proof of the stratum theorem, suppose there are at least two coefficients in (0,1). There is also the fixed negative coefficient -1. The density f of V=sum a_i E_i is positive, continuously differentiable, and log-concave on the whole real line. Zero coefficients are omitted. Positivity and smoothness follow by convolving two positive exponential phases with a negative exponential phase, and further convolution preserves them. Log-concavity follows from the convolution theorem for log-concave densities.

We use two proved facts, including their size-bias/Hessian identities, from `candidate 8704554a92158bfc`. For clarity, their exact relevant content is recalled here. If c>0, define

    phi_+(c)=f_(V+cE')(0)/f(0)
            =integral_0^infinity e^(-t/c) f(-t)/(c f(0)) dt.

Then psi_+=1/phi_+ is convex, psi_+(0+)=1, and

    psi_+(c)>=1 implies psi_+'(c)>0.                 (1)

The coefficient derivative is

    partial_i P=f_(V+a_i E')(0)>0,                  (2)

also when a_i<0. Holding the current density f fixed in the definition of phi_+, for two positive coordinates p_i,p_j the Hessian entries are

    P_ii=2 f(0) phi_+'(p_i),
    P_ij=f(0)[phi_+(p_i)-phi_+(p_j)]/(p_i-p_j),    (3)

with the quotient interpreted as phi_+' at repeated coefficients. The cited source proves these identities and (1) by elementary exponential convolution and a half-line log-concave moment inequality.

### Common derivative and the density at zero

Choose any free positive coordinate p and a free negative coordinate -b, where 0<p,b<1. Perturbing one coefficient upward and the other downward preserves the sum, and both signs remain unchanged for sufficiently small perturbations. Stationarity therefore implies that all coefficients strictly between -1 and 1, in particular every free positive and every free negative coefficient, have the same first derivative lambda. We need only these nonzero free coordinates, so zeros do not enter the argument. Put q=lambda/f(0)>0.

For a free positive p,

    phi_+(p)=q.

For a free negative -b, (2) gives

    phi_-(b):=integral_0^infinity e^(-t/b) f(t)/(b f(0)) dt=q.

We claim q<=1. Because log f is differentiable and concave, its derivative at zero controls one entire half-line. If f'(0)>=0, then for t>=0,

    log f(-t)<=log f(0)-t (log f)'(0)<=log f(0),

so phi_+(p)<=1. If f'(0)<=0, the same tangent inequality on the positive half-line gives f(t)<=f(0), hence phi_-(b)<=1. These cases exhaust all possibilities, proving q<=1. In fact q<1: on the chosen half-line f(t)<=f(0), and equality everywhere would contradict integrability. Continuity supplies a nonempty interval of strict inequality, and the exponential averaging density is positive there.

### Descending positive pair

Suppose p_i,p_j are two free positive coefficients. By (1), since phi_+(p_i)=phi_+(p_j)=q<=1,

    phi_+'(p_i)<0 and phi_+'(p_j)<0.

Perturb only this pair by p_i+s,p_j-s. This remains feasible for both signs of sufficiently small s, and its first derivative is zero.

If p_i!=p_j, their divided difference in (3) is zero; the second derivative along this line is

    2 f(0)[phi_+'(p_i)+phi_+'(p_j)]<0.

If p_i=p_j=p, the second derivative is instead

    2 f(0) phi_+'(p)<0.

In both cases Taylor's theorem contradicts local minimality. Thus at most one free positive coefficient can occur. This proves the theorem.

## The all-unit negative stratum

Suppose all nonzero negative coefficients equal -1, and let their number be m>=1. Then P>=1/2.

Here we invoke the proved density lemma in `candidate a6e6fd61fe60c16a` (independently audited): if Y=sum_j b_j E_j with 0<=b_j<=1 and sum_j b_j>=m, the density of Gamma(m,1)-Y has derivative <=0 at zero. Its reflected version says that the density of Y-Gamma(m,1) has derivative >=0 at zero.

Take a positive pair p_i>=p_j, both below one, and let

    W=V+p_i E_i'+p_j E_j'.

Its negative part is Gamma(m,1). All its positive coefficients are at most one and their sum is m+p_i+p_j>=m. Thus f_W'(0)>=0. The exact transfer identity is

    partial_i P-partial_j P=(p_j-p_i) f_W'(0)<=0.

Consequently increasing p_i and decreasing p_j by equal amounts cannot increase P, for as long as both remain in [0,1]. Repeat until at most one positive coefficient is fractional. The sum of the positive coefficients is the integer m, so no fractional coefficient can remain. The final positive sum is an independent Gamma(m,1), and its probability of exceeding the negative Gamma(m,1) is exactly 1/2. Every transfer was nonincreasing, proving the assertion.

For m=1, the same argument may be replaced by the direct formula

    P=1-product_i(1+p_i)^(-1)>=1/2,

because sum_i p_i=1 and product_i(1+p_i)>=2. Thus no density differentiability convention for Gamma shape one is required.

## Global reduction

Any minimizer on A_d is in one of the following classes:

1. all nonzero negatives are -1, in which case its probability is at least 1/2; or
2. its positive coefficients are k copies of 1, together with at most one coefficient p in (0,1).

The second conclusion follows from the free-sign stratum theorem. There must be at least one positive coefficient; because a_0=-1, their sum is at least one. In class 2 this forces k>=1. Other coefficients may be negative or zero, and the negative weights sum to k+p (with p=0 if there is no fractional positive).

This is a genuine finite-dimensional boundary-stratum reduction. It does not assert that arbitrary positive pairs can be merged, and it does not yet bound the class with one fractional positive coefficient.

## Stronger classification when a fractional positive occurs

Suppose a minimizer has a free positive p in (0,1) and a free negative coefficient. The preceding argument gives a common derivative ratio q<=1. For negative magnitudes set

    phi_-(b)=f_(V-bE')(0)/f(0), psi_-=1/phi_-.

Apply the reciprocal-Laplace lemma to h(t)=f(t)/f(0). It gives convexity of psi_-, the limit psi_-(0+)=1, and positive derivative wherever psi_->=1. Every free negative magnitude satisfies psi_-(b)=1/q>=1. This level can occur at only one positive b: if b1<b2 were two such points, positivity of psi_-'(b1) and convexity would imply psi_-(b2)>psi_-(b1). Hence all free negative magnitudes equal b.

There is no additional coefficient -1 besides the mandatory a_0=-1. Indeed, convexity and psi_-'(b)>0 imply psi_-(1)>psi_-(b), hence the derivative at any extra coefficient -1 is strictly less than lambda. Increase that coefficient by s>0 and decrease p by s. This is feasible for sufficiently small s, preserves the fixed a_0 and the sum, and has strictly negative first derivative. That contradicts minimality.

Consequently every minimizer with a fractional positive coefficient and any fractional negative coefficient has the form

    positive coefficients: k copies of 1 and one p in (0,1),
    negative coefficients: the fixed 1 and m copies of b in (0,1),
    remaining coefficients: zero,
    b=(k+p-1)/m, k>=1, m>=k.

This is an exact classification of that remaining stationary stratum, not a claim that every point of this family is stationary. In particular, the unresolved scalar family is

    P_{k,m}(p)=Pr(Gamma(k,1)+p Exp(1)
                 >=Exp(1)+[(k+p-1)/m] Gamma(m,1)),

with all random variables independent. Proving that this family has no interior local minimum below both endpoint values would remove the final fractional positive. That last assertion is not proved in this note.

## No zero coordinates in the fractional-positive stratum

The strict inequality q<1 also excludes any zero coefficient at such a minimizer. A zero coordinate has derivative f(0), while the free positive has derivative lambda=q f(0)<f(0). Increase p by s and make the zero coefficient -s. This is feasible for small s>0, preserves a_0 and the total sum, and has derivative lambda-f(0)<0. Hence no zero coefficient occurs. The number of coordinates is therefore exactly k+m+2=d+1, and m=d-k-1.
